L2t: The problem asks for contiguous substrings of a digit string, so the same digits at different positions count as separate substrings.
L3t: Subtract 1 from each digit so that the condition 'digit sum equals length' becomes 'sum of (digit-1) over the substring equals 0', then count pairs of equal prefix sums using a hash map.
L4t: Compute running prefix sums of (digit - 1) and use a dictionary of how often each prefix value has occurred, adding that frequency to the count at each position, which counts all zero-sum substrings in linear time.
L2f: Counting substrings of a digit string is usually done only for non-empty substrings, and the digits are always read as characters from the string.
L3f: Only substrings made entirely of the digit 1 can have a digit sum equal to their length, because any digit above 1 always pushes the sum past the length.
L4f: The answer is to count only the substrings made up entirely of the digit '1', by summing k*(k+1)/2 over each run of consecutive 1s.
